Fireman Leaves Trail of Smoke
ZA
Photo Courtesy of Midwest Racing News
Eddie Meyer, a lieutenant in the Glenview (Ill.) Fire Department, smoked up the scene with red-hot tires
when he spun in last September's 250 mile stock car race here. Going down low to miss Meyer's errant 1965
Dodge is Jim Martin of Fort Wayne, Ind., in a 1965 Plymouth. Heading straight for Meyer, but missing him at
the last moment was William "Whitey" Gerken of Melrose Park, Ill., in his #44 1966 Chevrolet. Meyer continued
in the race.

Scorers At Work
Charged with the responsibility of keeping the positions of the drivers in order at each major race at state
fair park is the crew of more than 50 trained scorers. Fred Williams and Christy Zwaagstra handle the scorers,
setting up their individual scoring charts and checking constantly with them as the race progresses. Each scorer
is assigned one of the cars in a race. As the car passes the scoring stand, the scorer checks the small timing
device and marks the total number of seconds it took the car to circle the track. On the next lap the timing
device then records the total elapsed time for the two laps. If the scorer misses his ( or her) assigned car on one
lap, the total elapsed time will indicate that there is a gap in the time. As each car comes around, the scorer
notes the total number of seconds and marks it in a space on the lap chart in front of him. Each scoring ehart
has the number of spaces to correspond with the number of miles in the race.
